2.modern-en: Appears at court still mourning his father. Bitterly resents his mother's hasty remarriage to Claudius. Agrees to stay in Denmark rather than return to Wittenberg. Learns from Horatio that a ghost resembling his father has appeared.

4.modern-en: Waits on the platform at midnight for the ghost. When it appears and beckons, he follows it despite his friends' warnings.

5.modern-en: The ghost reveals Claudius murdered his father by pouring poison in his ear. Hamlet swears revenge and makes Horatio and Marcellus swear secrecy. Declares he may put on an 'antic disposition.'

7.modern-en: Greets Rosencrantz and Guildenstern but quickly suspects they were sent by the King. Hears the players recite a speech about Priam's slaughter. Plans to use a play to test Claudius's guilt.

8.modern-en: Delivers the 'To be or not to be' soliloquy. Encounters Ophelia in what he suspects is a setup. Tells her to go to a nunnery and denies ever having loved her.

9.modern-en: Directs the players and instructs Horatio to watch Claudius during the play. The play-within-a-play ('The Mousetrap') causes Claudius to flee in guilt. Hamlet is now certain of the King's crime.

10.modern-en: Comes upon Claudius praying alone but decides not to kill him at prayer, wanting to catch him in sin so his soul won't be saved.

11.modern-en: Confronts his mother in her chamber, killing Polonius who was hiding behind the arras. The ghost appears again, visible only to Hamlet, urging him not to forget his purpose.

13.modern-en: Eludes Rosencrantz and Guildenstern, refusing to reveal where he has hidden Polonius's body.

14.modern-en: Brought before Claudius, he mocks the King with riddles about Polonius's body. Is sent to England, unaware that Claudius has ordered his execution there.

15.modern-en: Encounters Fortinbras's army marching to fight over a worthless patch of land. Reflects on his own inaction and resolves that from now on his thoughts will be bloody.

19.modern-en: Returns to Denmark and encounters gravediggers in a churchyard. Discovers Yorick's skull and meditates on death. Witnesses Ophelia's funeral and leaps into the grave in a confrontation with Laertes.

20.modern-en: Tells Horatio how he discovered and rewrote Claudius's death warrant, sending Rosencrantz and Guildenstern to their deaths. Accepts Laertes's fencing challenge. In the final duel, is wounded by the poisoned sword. After Gertrude drinks the poisoned cup and Laertes confesses, Hamlet kills Claudius and dies, naming Fortinbras as his successor.

2.modern-en: Opens court with a speech balancing grief for his dead brother with celebration of his new marriage and kingship. Grants Laertes permission to return to France. Asks Hamlet to stay in Denmark.

7.modern-en: Sends Rosencrantz and Guildenstern to spy on Hamlet and discover the cause of his strange behavior.

8.modern-en: Hides with Polonius to observe Hamlet's encounter with Ophelia. Concludes that Hamlet's behavior is not caused by love and decides to send him to England.

9.modern-en: Watches the play-within-a-play and rises in agitation when the murder scene mirrors his own crime, calling for lights.

10.modern-en: Attempts to pray, confessing his guilt over murdering his brother. Admits he cannot truly repent because he still possesses the gains of his crime — the crown and the queen.

12.modern-en: Learns from Gertrude that Hamlet has killed Polonius. Fears for his own life and resolves to send Hamlet to England immediately.

14.modern-en: Confronts Hamlet about Polonius's body. Sends him to England with secret letters ordering his execution.

16.modern-en: Deals with the crisis of Laertes storming the castle with a mob, demanding answers about his father's death. Calms Laertes and begins turning him against Hamlet.

18.modern-en: Plots with Laertes to kill Hamlet using a poisoned sword in a fencing match, with a poisoned cup as a backup plan.

20.modern-en: Watches the duel unfold. When Gertrude accidentally drinks the poisoned cup, he fails to stop her. Is exposed by the dying Laertes and killed by Hamlet with the poisoned sword and forced to drink the remaining poison.

2.modern-en: Asks Hamlet to stay in Denmark and stop mourning so visibly for his father.

8.modern-en: Present at Claudius's plan to observe Hamlet with Ophelia, hoping love is the cause of his madness.

9.modern-en: Watches the play-within-a-play. Hamlet asks her how she likes the play; she replies the Player Queen protests too much.

11.modern-en: Confronted by Hamlet in her chamber. Witnesses Hamlet kill Polonius. Is forced to see the moral ugliness of her marriage to Claudius. Agrees to keep Hamlet's sanity a secret.

12.modern-en: Reports Polonius's death to Claudius, distressed and shaken.

16.modern-en: Tries to calm Laertes when he storms the castle. Witnesses Ophelia's madness with grief.

18.modern-en: Brings news that Ophelia has drowned.

20.modern-en: Drinks from the poisoned cup despite Claudius's feeble attempts to stop her. Dies, warning Hamlet the drink is poisoned.

3.modern-en: Receives advice from Laertes about Hamlet's affections, warning her not to trust his love. Polonius forbids her from seeing Hamlet.

6.modern-en: Reports to Polonius that Hamlet came to her looking wild and distracted, grabbing her wrist and staring at her face before leaving with a sigh.

8.modern-en: Is used as bait in Claudius and Polonius's trap. Tries to return Hamlet's gifts. Endures his cruel rejection and his command to go to a nunnery. Left heartbroken.

9.modern-en: Sits beside Hamlet at the play. Endures his crude, sexually suggestive comments.

16.modern-en: Appears mad, singing incoherent songs about death, loss, and betrayal. Distributes flowers with symbolic meanings to the court.

epithet.en: Lord Chamberlain, father of Laertes and Ophelia

2.modern-en: Present at court. Supports Laertes's request to return to France.

3.modern-en: Gives Laertes his famous farewell advice ('to thine own self be true'). Forbids Ophelia from seeing Hamlet, declaring his vows are mere traps.

6.modern-en: Sends Reynaldo to Paris to spy on Laertes. Hears Ophelia's report of Hamlet's strange visit and concludes Hamlet is mad with love.

7.modern-en: Presents his theory that Hamlet is mad for love of Ophelia. Plans to use Ophelia to prove it, with himself hidden to observe.

8.modern-en: Hides with Claudius to spy on Hamlet's encounter with Ophelia.

9.modern-en: Introduces the players before the performance. Makes himself a target of Hamlet's mockery.

10.modern-en: Tells Claudius he will hide behind the arras in Gertrude's chamber to spy on Hamlet's conversation with his mother.

11.modern-en: Hides behind the arras in the Queen's chamber. Cries out when Gertrude seems threatened and is stabbed through the curtain by Hamlet, who mistakes him for Claudius.

epithet.en: Hamlet's loyal friend and fellow scholar

1.modern-en: Arrives at the watch skeptical but witnesses the ghost himself. Recognizes it resembles the dead King and speculates it portends trouble for Denmark.

2.modern-en: Reports the ghost sighting to Hamlet and agrees to watch with him that night.

4.modern-en: Tries to restrain Hamlet from following the ghost, fearing it may lead him to danger.

5.modern-en: Swears secrecy about the ghost at Hamlet's insistence.

9.modern-en: Assigned by Hamlet to watch Claudius during the play and confirm his guilty reaction.

16.modern-en: Witnesses Ophelia's madness and receives sailors bearing a letter from Hamlet about his return.

17.modern-en: Reads Hamlet's letter revealing how he escaped the ship to England by boarding a pirate vessel.

19.modern-en: Accompanies Hamlet to the graveyard. Listens to his reflections on mortality.

20.modern-en: Hears Hamlet's account of rewriting the death warrant. Witnesses the final duel and catastrophe. Tries to drink the remaining poison to die with Hamlet but is stopped. Entrusted with telling Hamlet's story to the world.

epithet.en: Son of Polonius, brother of Ophelia

2.modern-en: Asks for and receives permission to return to France.

3.modern-en: Warns Ophelia not to trust Hamlet's declarations of love before departing for France.

16.modern-en: Returns from France in a rage, storms the castle with a mob, and demands to know who killed his father. Sees Ophelia's madness and is devastated.

18.modern-en: Plots with Claudius to kill Hamlet with a poisoned, sharpened sword during a fencing match.

19.modern-en: Confronts Hamlet at Ophelia's grave, grappling with him in grief and fury.

20.modern-en: Duels Hamlet and wounds him with the poisoned blade, but is also cut with the same weapon when swords are exchanged. Dying, he confesses the plot and blames Claudius, then asks Hamlet's forgiveness.

1.modern-en: Appears twice on the battlements in full armor, resembling the dead King Hamlet. Refuses to speak and vanishes at the cock's crow.

4.modern-en: Appears again and beckons Hamlet to follow it away from his companions.

5.modern-en: Reveals that Claudius murdered him by pouring poison in his ear while he slept in the garden. Commands Hamlet to avenge him but spare Gertrude.

11.modern-en: Appears in Gertrude's chamber, visible only to Hamlet. Urges him to comfort his frightened mother and not to forget the mission of revenge.

epithet.en: Courtier and former schoolfriend of Hamlet

7.modern-en: Arrives at court with Guildenstern, sent by Claudius and Gertrude to discover the cause of Hamlet's madness.

8.modern-en: Reports to Claudius that Hamlet remains evasive but seems interested in the visiting players.

9.modern-en: Attempts to get Hamlet to confide in him after the play. Hamlet accuses him of trying to play him like a pipe.

10.modern-en: Agrees with Guildenstern to escort Hamlet to England, expressing loyalty to the King.

12.modern-en: Sent with Guildenstern to find Hamlet and recover Polonius's body.

13.modern-en: Tries to get Hamlet to reveal where he hid Polonius's body.

14.modern-en: Escorts Hamlet toward England, carrying Claudius's sealed orders.

15.modern-en: Accompanies Hamlet on the march, unaware of the death warrant he carries.

epithet.en: Courtier and former schoolfriend of Hamlet

7.modern-en: Arrives with Rosencrantz at court to investigate Hamlet's behavior.

8.modern-en: Reports to the King alongside Rosencrantz about their failed attempt to discover what troubles Hamlet.

9.modern-en: Summoned by Hamlet after the play. Hamlet challenges him about attempting to manipulate him.

10.modern-en: Pledges to accompany Hamlet to England, speaking of the duty to protect the King.

12.modern-en: Sent to find Hamlet after Polonius's death.

15.modern-en: Leads his army through Denmark on the way to fight over a small patch of Polish ground. His captain explains the insignificance of the territory.

20.modern-en: Arrives at Elsinore to find the royal family dead. Claims the Danish throne with Hamlet's dying endorsement. Orders a soldier's funeral for Hamlet.

epithet.en: A clown who digs graves at the churchyard

19.modern-en: Digs Ophelia's grave while joking with his companion about whether she deserves a Christian burial. Engages Hamlet in witty banter about death and produces Yorick's skull.

20.modern-en: Delivers the fencing challenge from Claudius in an absurdly flowery manner. Hamlet mocks his affected speech before accepting the wager.
